intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the most spectacular highlights including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. Trek through ancient lenga beech forests, past turquoise lakes, and beneath dramatic granite peaks. Book refugios or campsites along the route for an immersive backcountry experience.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Witness the legendary alpenglow as the rising sun paints the towers in shades of gold and pink reflected in the glacial lagoon below. This is one of Patagonia's most breathtaking and rewarding natural spectacles, best experienced in the early morning light.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector of Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters of Lago Grey toward the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most accessible glaciers. Navigate between luminous blue icebergs calved from the glacier face while a certified guide explains the glaciology and ecology of the region. A thrilling way to experience the raw power of Patagonian ice up close from water level.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Sector of Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés (French Valley) Trek
experiences.description: Hike into the dramatic French Valley, a glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and jagged peaks including Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice avalanches tumbling from the glaciers above as you ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a panoramic 360-degree view of the park's most dramatic scenery.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife & Pampas Nature Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk across the open pampas and lakeshores of the park's eastern sector to spot Patagonia's incredible wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, rheas, flamingos, and pumas in their natural habitat. An expert naturalist guide provides deep ecological insight into the Patagonian steppe ecosystem and the park's conservation efforts, making this a perfect complement to the high-intensity trekking days.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga & Eastern Pampas, Torres del Paine

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget transfer or shared shuttle to accommodation near Torres del Paine. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: Airport food court or packed snacks from home
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a 24-hour convenience store near arrival area before heading to the resort

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival — do not plan any outdoor activities. Confirm shuttle booking in advance to save costs vs. private taxi. Pack snacks for the journey. Get to bed early to prepare for the trek-heavy days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After breakfast, orient yourself around the Aegean Bliss Resort and the surrounding area. Visit the park entrance or nearby visitor center to pick up free trail maps, check current trail conditions, and purchase your Torres del Paine National Park entrance pass (budget for approximately $35–45 USD for international visitors).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely introductory walk along the shores of Lago del Toro or a nearby easy nature trail close to the resort. Observe local birdlife including Andean condors, flamingos, and upland geese. This gentle hike serves as acclimatization for the bigger treks ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Organize and pack your trekking gear for the coming days. Review the W Trek or O Circuit route options and plan your camping or refugio strategy to keep costs low.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or self-prepared oats and fruit from supplies bought at a local supermarket in Puerto Natales
meals.lunch: Packed sandwich and fruit from supplies — eat at a scenic lakeside spot
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice meal using the resort kitchen facilities or camp kitchen to save money

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on 5–7 days of trail food (energy bars, dried pasta, instant soups, nuts, crackers) at a supermarket in Puerto Natales before entering the park — food inside the park is very expensive. Keep receipts for park entry.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Wake at 04:00 and begin the 4–5 hour ascent from the Hostería Las Torres trailhead. The trail climbs through lenga beech forest and rocky moraine to reach the iconic base of the three granite towers at sunrise. Bring layers, headlamp, and a thermos of hot tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the same trail back to the trailhead (approximately 3–4 hours). The descent offers stunning views of the valley and Lago Nordenskjöld. Rest your legs and rehydrate at the bottom.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shuttle or on foot. Shower, stretch, and rest tired muscles. Prepare and organize gear for the next day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy bars, nuts, and instant coffee consumed before the hike at 04:00
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at the mirador — sandwiches, dried fruit, chocolate, and nuts
meals.dinner: Hot homemade soup and bread at the resort kitchen — a warming budget-friendly meal after a long day

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic hike in Torres del Paine. Start before dawn to catch sunrise at the towers. The round trip is approximately 18–22 km with 800m elevation gain — wear proper hiking boots and carry at least 2 liters of water. Weather can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the demanding Las Torres hike. Sleep in, do light stretching or yoga near the resort. Spend time journaling, reading, or photographing the stunning Patagonian landscape around the accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short and scenic walk to Lago Sarmiento, a stunning turquoise lake with unique stromatolite formations along its shores. This is an easy flat walk ideal for a rest day. Watch for guanacos and rheas in the surrounding steppe.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost park ranger talk or interpretive session if available at the visitor center. Plan logistics for the Valle del Francés trek coming up. Repack your bag and prepare a packed lunch for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with dried fruit and instant coffee — self-prepared
meals.lunch: Crackers with peanut butter, cheese, and fruit at Lago Sarmiento
meals.dinner: Lentil stew or canned bean meal cooked at the resort — hearty and cheap

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential in Patagonia to avoid injury. Use this day to air out hiking boots, dry damp gear, and treat any blisters. Lago Sarmiento is free to visit and strikingly beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Valle del Francés (French Valley) Trek. Take the early morning catamaran or bus from the resort area to reach the trailhead at Camping Italiano. Begin the ascent into the glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, soaring granite walls, and roaring waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to Mirador Británico, the highest viewpoint in the French Valley, offering panoramic views of Paine Grande, Los Cuernos, and multiple hanging glaciers. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving ice. Eat lunch at the mirador before beginning the descent.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to the valley floor and arrange return transport to the resort. Arrive back tired but exhilarated. Cook a hot meal and get to bed early.

meals.breakfast: Quick oats and coffee before departure — eaten at the resort
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Mirador Británico — energy bars, nuts, dried mango, and a wrap
meals.dinner: Pasta with canned tomato sauce and tuna cooked at the resort kitchen

day_by_day.notes: The Valle del Francés round trip is approximately 22–24 km. The catamaran crossing can be costly — check for budget ferry options or hike the connector trail if physically prepared. Start early to avoid afternoon Patagonian winds which can be fierce.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the area around Lago Grey and hike the trail toward Grey Glacier viewpoint. The trail offers stunning views of the massive blue glacier and floating icebergs in the lake. This is a moderate 4–6 hour round trip hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the glacier viewpoint and spend time watching icebergs drift across the milky blue lake. On clear days the views extend to the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Begin the return hike in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Wash clothes by hand and hang to dry. Resupply snacks and trail food if needed. Plan the upcoming days and consider any optional day trips.

meals.breakfast: Scrambled eggs and toast — self-prepared at the resort
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — cheese and crackers, nuts, chocolate bar
meals.dinner: Rice and beans with canned vegetables — simple, filling, and budget-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Do not attempt to touch or collect glacier ice — it is dangerous and prohibited. The Grey Glacier hike is less crowded than Las Torres and equally spectacular. Bring sunscreen and sunglasses as glacier glare is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free or low-cost self-guided walk along the Río Paine circuit near the resort. Look for Andean condors soaring on thermals, Darwin's rheas running across the steppe, and guanacos grazing near the riverbanks. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé. The short 20-minute walk from the parking area is free and highly rewarding. Spend time photographing the turquoise rushing water against the dramatic mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Midsummer solstice evening — enjoy the extraordinarily long Patagonian daylight (sunset around 22:00 in December). Sit outside with a hot drink and watch the alpenglow turn the Paine Massif pink and gold.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, granola, and fruit — purchased from a local store
meals.lunch: Picnic at Salto Grande — packed wraps and fruit
meals.dinner: Celebrate the solstice with a slightly upgraded meal — try a local empanada from a nearby food vendor or small restaurant as a treat

day_by_day.notes: December 21 is the summer solstice in the Southern Hemisphere — the longest day of the year. Patagonia enjoys up to 17–18 hours of daylight, making evening hikes and photography exceptional. No extra park fee for Salto Grande.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend time writing in a travel journal, editing photos, or simply relaxing and absorbing the scenery from the resort. Patagonia rewards those who slow down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day guided nature walk if a free or low-cost ranger-led option is available, or self-guide along the Mirador Cuernos trail for views of the dramatic Los Cuernos (The Horns) rock formations. This is a moderate 3–4 hour round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a celebratory group dinner at the resort kitchen if traveling with others, or treat yourself to a local Patagonian lamb stew (cordero) at the most affordable restaurant nearby as a mid-trip reward.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes made from a simple mix — a comfort breakfast mid-trip
meals.lunch: Soup and bread from resort supplies
meals.dinner: Budget splurge — local Patagonian lamb or a hearty stew at a nearby affordable eatery (budget $15–20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Los Cuernos are among the most photographed formations in Patagonia. The late afternoon light hits them beautifully. This is a good day to charge all electronics and back up photos.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a full-day hike along the northern section of the W Trek toward Campamento Torres and beyond. Explore lesser-visited side trails branching off the main route for solitude and wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the trail enjoying views of Lago Nordenskjöld and the back side of the Paine Massif. Look for pumas in the rocky hillsides — Torres del Paine has one of the highest puma densities in the world and December sightings are possible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort before dark (which is very late in December). Debrief the day, treat any sore spots, and begin mentally preparing for the final trekking days.

meals.breakfast: Oats and coffee — quick and early
meals.lunch: Full packed trail lunch — substantial sandwich, energy bars, dried fruit, nuts
meals.dinner: Instant noodles upgraded with canned tuna, soy sauce, and a boiled egg — satisfying trail dinner

day_by_day.notes: Puma sightings are most likely at dawn and dusk near rocky terrain and guanaco grazing areas. Never approach a puma. Report sightings to park rangers. Carry a whistle and know basic wildlife safety protocols.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — begin the day with a sunrise walk near the resort to watch the first light hit the Paine Massif. Take a short exploratory hike to a nearby viewpoint or lakeside area for quiet reflection and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a relaxed self-guided botanical walk, identifying Patagonian flora including calafate berries (legend says eating one ensures your return to Patagonia), coirón grasses, and native wildflowers in full December bloom.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration — prepare a festive shared meal at the resort kitchen. Splurge slightly on local wine (Chilean wine is excellent and affordable), cheese, and local snacks. Enjoy the long summer evening outdoors under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve breakfast — eggs, toast, jam, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Light lakeside picnic with calafate berry snacks if found on the trail
meals.dinner: Festive budget dinner — pasta with a rich sauce, local wine, and chocolate for dessert (budget $10–15 USD in supplies)

day_by_day.notes: Calafate berries ripen in January–February but you may find some in late December. They are edible and delicious. Chilean supermarket wine (Carménère or Malbec) costs $5–8 USD and pairs perfectly with a Patagonian evening.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — take a memorable sunrise hike to a favorite viewpoint discovered during the trip. Bring hot chocolate or coffee in a thermos and watch the Patagonian dawn in peaceful solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final full afternoon in Torres del Paine — revisit your favorite trail or viewpoint. Spend time sitting quietly in nature, absorbing the scale and wildness of this extraordinary landscape. Begin packing non-essential gear.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at the resort — organize all gear, do final laundry, and pack bags for departure. Write down top memories and lessons from the trip. Enjoy a final meal and toast to a successful Patagonian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast — use remaining supplies creatively for a feast
meals.lunch: Final trail picnic at a scenic spot — use up remaining packed food
meals.dinner: Splurge on a final dinner at a local restaurant or prepare the best meal of the trip from remaining supplies. Try local curanto or cazuela if available nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Many services may be reduced on Christmas Day. Confirm transport and any bookings for the following day's departure in advance. Tip resort staff if service has been good — a small gesture goes a long way.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake early for one last look at the Paine Massif from the resort. Take a short 30-minute walk to say goodbye to the landscape. Complete all packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from the resort to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas for onward travel. Use the journey time to reflect on the trip, organize photos, and rest. If time allows before your flight, explore Puerto Natales town center, visit the free Museo Histórico, and pick up affordable local souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. Board your return flight or onward transport. Carry calafate berry jam or local Chilean products as affordable, meaningful gifts.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before checkout — use any remaining supplies
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch in Puerto Natales — try a local almuerzo (set lunch menu) for $8–12 USD at a family restaurant
meals.dinner: Airport food or packed snacks for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: The almuerzo del día (daily set lunch) at local restaurants in Puerto Natales typically includes soup, a main course, and a drink for under $10 USD — the best value meal in Chilean Patagonia. Allow extra time for the drive to Punta Arenas airport (3+ hours from Torres del Paine). Do not cut it close.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, unpack essentials, and review the trip plan for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at the airport before departure, or enjoy a late welcome drink and light bites at the resort's bar if available upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Confirm transfer pickup in advance. Keep a snack and water bottle in your carry-on for the late-night journey to the resort. The drive from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine can take 1.5–2.5 hours depending on road conditions. Rest well – big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning getting oriented – visit the park's entrance, collect your park permit, and pick up trail maps. Stroll around the resort's beachfront area to take in your first views of the Patagonian landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided Patagonian Wildlife & Pampas Nature Walk in the eastern sector of the park. This gentle 2–3 hour guided walk introduces you to the park's open pampas, lakeshores, and local fauna including guanacos, ñandus (rheas), Andean condors, and flamingos. Perfect for acclimatization without heavy exertion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a warm shower. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant. Review gear and pack for upcoming hikes. Early bedtime recommended.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – fuel up with eggs, fresh bread, local jams, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light meal at a park visitor center café during the nature walk.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant – try a classic Patagonian lamb stew (cordero al palo) or grilled trout with local vegetables. Mid-range pricing expected at resort.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase or confirm your Torres del Paine National Park entrance pass (CONAF) – fees apply for foreign visitors. Tipping guides is customary (approx. 10–15%). Weather in Patagonia changes rapidly; always carry a waterproof layer, sunscreen, and wind jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Wake at 04:00 and depart by 04:30 to reach the trailhead at Hostería Las Torres. Begin the 4–5 hour round-trip hike through lenga beech forest and up the famous boulder field moraine to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Arrive at the mirador around sunrise (approximately 06:00–07:00 in December) for golden light on the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the mirador back to the trailhead (2–2.5 hours). Rest legs, enjoy a hot drink at the Hostería Las Torres café. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for lunch and a short afternoon rest. Optional: gentle lakeside stroll near the resort to stretch legs.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Light stretching or yoga to recover muscles. Dinner at the resort or a nearby local restaurant in the park area.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy snack at 04:00 (energy bars, fruit, nuts from resort or self-prepared). Proper hot breakfast upon return to resort post-hike.
meals.lunch: Hot soup and sandwich at Hostería Las Torres café after descending, or packed lunch from resort.
meals.dinner: Dinner at resort restaurant – opt for a protein-rich meal such as grilled beef or salmon to aid muscle recovery.

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most iconic hikes in South America. The total round trip is approximately 18–20 km with 800m elevation gain. Wear proper hiking boots with ankle support. The boulder field near the top is steep and requires careful footing. Bring at least 2 liters of water, sunscreen, and layers. December daylight is long (18+ hours) but pre-dawn start is essential for sunrise views.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a full breakfast at the resort. Light activity only – take a leisurely walk along the beachfront or resort grounds. Review gear, re-pack bags, and prepare for the upcoming W Trek multi-day hike starting tomorrow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the CONAF park administration office or visitor center for a detailed W Trek briefing. Confirm refugio/camping reservations (book well in advance – essential in December high season). Stop at a gear shop in Puerto Natales or park area to pick up any missing supplies: blister pads, trekking poles, freeze-dried meals, or extra layers.
day_by_day.evening: Final preparation for the W Trek. Lay out and pack your trekking bag. Dinner at the resort with a hearty, carb-loading meal. Early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – take your time and eat well.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local café or restaurant near the park visitor center – try a classic Chilean empanada and fresh juice.
meals.dinner: Hearty carb-focused dinner at the resort – pasta, rice dishes, or traditional cazuela (Chilean stew) to fuel the upcoming multi-day trek.

day_by_day.notes: W Trek refugio reservations with Vertice Patagonia or Las Torres Patagonia must be booked months in advance during December high season. Confirm all bookings today. Pack only essentials for the trek – most refugios offer basic meals and sleeping bags for rent, reducing pack weight. Consider a mid-range refugio package that includes breakfast and dinner for budget efficiency.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 1: Depart Aegean Bliss Resort early. Take the catamaran or ferry across Lago Pehoé to Refugio Paine Grande (the western starting point of the W). Arrive mid-morning and drop bags at the refugio. Begin trekking toward Glacier Grey – hike 2.5–3 hours along the lakeside trail with stunning views of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Mirador Grey viewpoint for close-up views of the Grey Glacier's towering blue ice face. Explore the shoreline and watch for calving icebergs in Lago Grey. Return to Refugio Grey (approximately 11 km from Paine Grande) for the night.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Grey. Check in, hot shower (available at refugio), and relax. Communal dinner at the refugio dining hall with fellow trekkers. Share stories and review tomorrow's route.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the trail with glacier views – sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit.
meals.dinner: Set dinner menu at Refugio Grey – typically includes soup, main course (pasta or meat), and dessert. Included in refugio package or purchased separately (~$30–40 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran from Pudeto to Refugio Paine Grande runs on a schedule – confirm departure times in advance (typically 09:00 and 12:00 in high season). Total trekking distance today: approximately 22 km round trip to glacier and back to refugio. Pack rain gear – the Grey Glacier area is particularly prone to sudden weather changes and strong winds.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 2: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition. After breakfast at Refugio Grey, join a guided kayaking expedition on Lago Grey. Paddle through iceberg-dotted turquoise waters toward the massive Grey Glacier face. Guides provide safety briefing and equipment. Paddle duration: approximately 3–4 hours with stops to observe floating icebergs up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return kayaks and rest briefly at the refugio. Begin trekking back eastward toward Refugio Paine Grande (11 km, approximately 3 hours). Enjoy panoramic views of the Paine Massif and surrounding peaks on the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Paine Grande. Check in and rest. Communal dinner at the refugio. Prepare gear for tomorrow's French Valley trek.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Grey breakfast – hot porridge, bread, eggs, coffee, and juice.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on kayak or trail – energy-dense snacks, sandwiches provided or self-prepared.
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Paine Grande dining hall – warming soup and hearty main course.

day_by_day.notes: Grey Glacier kayaking is a premium experience – book in advance through Big Foot Patagonia or similar operators (~$80–120 USD per person). Dry bags are provided but keep valuables in a waterproof case. Hypothermia risk is real in these waters; follow all guide instructions. Wetsuits and paddle jackets are provided.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 3: Valle del Francés (French Valley) Trek. Depart Refugio Paine Grande early for the French Valley, one of the most dramatic sections of the W Trek. Hike 2–3 hours through lenga beech forest along Río del Francés. Ascend into the glacially carved amphitheater of the French Valley with towering hanging glaciers on all sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the upper French Valley mirador (Mirador Británico or Mirador del Francés) for breathtaking 360-degree views of hanging glaciers, granite spires, and the Paine Massif. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving ice. Descend back to the valley floor and continue east along the trail to Refugio Los Cuernos.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos with iconic views of Los Cuernos del Paine reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld. Enjoy a well-earned rest, hot shower, and communal dinner. Celebrate the halfway point of the W Trek.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande – hot coffee and full meal before long trekking day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the upper French Valley mirador with one of the most spectacular views in Patagonia.
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos – often considered one of the better refugio meals on the W Trek.

day_by_day.notes: Today is the longest and most strenuous day of the W Trek – approximately 25–28 km total. An early start (07:00) is essential. The upper French Valley trail beyond Mirador del Francés is optional and adds 2+ hours; assess energy levels before committing. Wind gusts in the valley can be extreme – secure all loose gear and clothing.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 4: Eastern Sector Trek. Depart Refugio Los Cuernos after breakfast. Trek eastward along the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld toward Refugio Chileno (approximately 11 km, 3–4 hours). Enjoy stunning views of Los Cuernos peaks and the turquoise lake. The trail winds through mixed terrain of forest, open pampas, and rocky ridgelines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Chileno by early afternoon. Rest and refuel. Optional short afternoon hike to a nearby mirador for views of the Torres del Paine towers from a different angle. Prepare mentally and physically for tomorrow's final sunrise hike.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner at Refugio Chileno. Briefing with refugio staff on tomorrow's pre-dawn departure for the Torres viewpoint. Set alarms for 04:00. Early bedtime by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on trail – simple sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, and dried fruit.
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Refugio Chileno – eat well and hydrate fully for tomorrow's final push.

day_by_day.notes: Refugio Chileno is the last stop before the Torres viewpoint. Confirm your alarm and departure time with other trekkers or refugio staff. Pack only essentials in a small daypack for the final ascent tomorrow – leave main pack at the refugio. Weather forecast check is crucial tonight for tomorrow's sunrise conditions.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 5 (Final Day): Pre-dawn rise at 04:00. Light breakfast and depart Refugio Chileno by 04:30 for the final ascent to Mirador Las Torres. This is a different approach than Day 3 (coming from the refugio side). Hike 2–2.5 hours up through forest and the final boulder field moraine to the iconic viewpoint. Watch the sunrise paint the granite towers in shades of orange and gold.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the Torres viewpoint (1.5–2 hours) to the main trailhead at Hostería Las Torres. Collect main pack from Refugio Chileno en route or arrange transfer. Celebrate completing the W Trek with a hot meal at Hostería Las Torres restaurant. Arrange transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort – hot shower, laundry, and full relaxation. Celebratory dinner at a nicer restaurant to mark the completion of the W Trek. Reflect on the journey.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy snack at 04:00 (bars, banana, coffee from refugio thermos). Hot breakfast at Hostería Las Torres restaurant after descending.
meals.lunch: Hearty lunch at Hostería Las Torres – treat yourself to a proper meal after 5 days on the trail.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the resort or a recommended local restaurant – splurge slightly on a parrilla (Patagonian BBQ) with grilled lamb, beef, and local wines.

day_by_day.notes: Completing the W Trek is a major achievement – approximately 80 km over 5 days. Hot showers at the resort will feel extraordinary. Treat any blisters or muscle soreness promptly. Wash and dry all trekking gear for potential reuse. Book a celebratory dinner reservation in advance if possible during high season.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Sleep in as late as needed. Gentle stretching or a short yoga session on the beachfront. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort with no agenda. Read, journal, or simply sit and absorb the Patagonian landscape from the resort's beachfront area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional light activity: Take a short, flat nature walk near the resort along the lakeshore to spot wildlife (guanacos, condors, flamingos) without any strenuous effort. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's facilities – lounge areas, reading room, or spa treatments if available. Visit the resort's viewpoint for panoramic photography of the Paine Massif.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner at the resort – many Patagonian lodges offer a special holiday dinner on December 24th. Enjoy a festive meal with local wines, traditional Chilean holiday dishes, and the company of fellow travelers. Stargazing on the beachfront if skies are clear (Patagonia offers exceptional dark skies).

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the resort – try everything on the menu.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café – fresh salad, soup, and local bread.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at the resort – expect a set menu with multiple courses, local Patagonian lamb, and Chilean wine. Budget for a slightly elevated spend on this special occasion (~$50–70 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: December 24th is Nochebuena (Christmas Eve) in Chile – a major celebration. The resort will likely have special programming. This is a perfect rest day between the W Trek and the final active days ahead. Hydrate well and eat nutritiously to continue recovery. Celebrate the journey so far.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day – Patagonian Wildlife & Pampas Nature Walk (second guided experience). Join a morning guided walk through the park's eastern sector pampas. This Christmas morning walk offers a fresh perspective on the park's ecosystems with a focus on birdwatching and wildlife photography. Spot guanacos with young calves (December is birthing season), Andean foxes, and a variety of migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a Christmas lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure – photography walk around the resort's beachfront, reading, or a relaxed paddle/boat trip on the lake if offered by the resort. Optional: visit a nearby lookout point for a final panoramic view of the full Paine Massif.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at the resort – a festive celebration with fellow guests. Share travel stories, enjoy local wines (try a Carménère from the Maipo Valley), and toast to an unforgettable Patagonian Christmas. Early preparation for tomorrow's final full day.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning breakfast at the resort – festive spread with local specialties.
meals.lunch: Christmas lunch at the resort – traditional Chilean holiday meal featuring roast lamb, potato dishes, and seasonal salads.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at the resort restaurant – multi-course festive menu with Chilean wine pairing. A special and memorable meal in one of the world's most spectacular settings.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is a magical experience – the long summer daylight means golden light well into the evening. Many park facilities may have reduced hours on December 25th; confirm guided walk availability in advance. This is one of the most memorable ways to spend Christmas – embrace the unique experience fully.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake early for a last sunrise walk along the resort's beachfront. Pack bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a final drive through the park for last views of the Paine Massif, stop at a scenic viewpoint for farewell photographs of the towers, condors, and Patagonian steppe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas for onward travel. If time permits before transfer, explore Puerto Natales town: browse local artisan shops for Patagonian wool products, leather goods, and souvenirs. Visit a local café for a final Chilean coffee and medialunas (croissants). Check in for onward flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days of trekking, wildlife, glaciers, and Patagonian wilderness. Carry memories of the W Trek, Grey Glacier, French Valley, and Torres del Paine sunrise for a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – eat well before the journey home.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales – try a local parilla restaurant or traditional Chilean almuerzo (set lunch menu) for an authentic and affordable farewell meal (~$12–18 USD).
meals.dinner: Airport dinner in Punta Arenas or onboard flight meal – pick up local chocolates or regional products as gifts at the airport shops.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample transfer time – the drive from Torres del Paine to Puerto Natales is approximately 1.5–2.5 hours, and Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas airport is an additional 3 hours. Confirm transfer and flight times carefully. December 26th (Boxing Day) is not a Chilean holiday, so all services operate normally. Consider shipping heavy trekking gear home to avoid airline baggage fees if continuing travel.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the most spectacular highlights including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. Trek through ancient lenga beech forests, past turquoise lakes, and beneath dramatic granite peaks. Book refugios or campsites along the route for an immersive backcountry experience.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Witness the legendary alpenglow as the rising sun paints the towers in shades of gold and pink reflected in the glacial lagoon below. This is one of Patagonia's most breathtaking and rewarding natural spectacles, best experienced in the early morning light.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector of Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters of Lago Grey toward the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most accessible glaciers. Navigate between luminous blue icebergs calved from the glacier face while a certified guide explains the glaciology and ecology of the region. A thrilling way to experience the raw power of Patagonian ice up close from water level.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Sector of Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés (French Valley) Trek
experiences.description: Hike into the dramatic French Valley, a glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and jagged peaks including Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice avalanches tumbling from the glaciers above as you ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a panoramic 360-degree view of the park's most dramatic scenery.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife & Pampas Nature Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk across the open pampas and lakeshores of the park's eastern sector to spot Patagonia's incredible wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, rheas, flamingos, and pumas in their natural habitat. An expert naturalist guide provides deep ecological insight into the Patagonian steppe ecosystem and the park's conservation efforts, making this a perfect complement to the high-intensity trekking days.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga & Eastern Pampas, Torres del Paine

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort picks you up in a heated, comfortable vehicle. Scenic night drive to the resort with a welcome champagne en route. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A – Travel Day
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Light welcome amenity prepared by the resort upon arrival – charcuterie board, local cheeses, Patagonian lamb empanadas, and a glass of premium Carménère wine waiting in your suite.

day_by_day.notes: Given the 22:30 arrival, no activities are scheduled. Ensure all gear and trekking equipment is confirmed with the resort concierge tonight for the days ahead. Rest is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort's panoramic restaurant overlooking the lake. Orientation session with the resort's private Patagonian guide – review the 12-day plan, gear check, and introduction to Torres del Paine National Park's ecosystems, flora, and fauna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Patagonian Wildlife & Pampas Nature Walk – Join your private guide for a gentle 2–3 hour introductory nature walk across the open pampas and lakeshores near the park's eastern sector. Spot guanacos, Darwin's rheas, Andean condors, flamingos, and possibly pumas in their natural habitat. This easy walk serves as a perfect acclimatization activity after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour on the private terrace with panoramic views of the Paine Massif. Enjoy a curated pisco sour and local craft beer tasting.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast buffet at the resort – fresh-baked medialunas, local berry preserves, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed calafate juice.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort's chef, served alfresco during the nature walk – artisan sandwiches, quinoa salad, fresh fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant featuring Patagonian king crab bisque, slow-roasted guanaco loin, and a calafate berry soufflé paired with a curated Chilean wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery and orientation day. Hydrate well and go to bed early to prepare for more demanding hikes ahead. Confirm sunrise hike logistics with the guide.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike – Wake at 03:30 for a private pre-dawn transfer to the Las Torres trailhead. Begin the 4–5 hour guided ascent through lenga beech forests and boulder fields in the dark with high-quality headlamps. Arrive at the iconic turquoise glacial lake at the base of the three granite towers just as the first golden light strikes the peaks – an unforgettable Patagonian moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend at a comfortable pace, pausing for wildlife spotting and photography. Return to the resort by early afternoon for a well-deserved rest, hot shower, and optional spa treatment (massage or hydrotherapy).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Private sunset viewing from the beachfront terrace with a sommelier-guided wine tasting featuring three premium Chilean and Argentine Patagonian wines.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy box prepared by the resort at 03:30 – protein bars, fresh fruit, thermos of hot coffee, and oat cookies.
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at the Mirador – the resort chef prepares an insulated bento-style box with smoked trout, roasted vegetable wraps, dark chocolate, and herbal tea.
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the resort – choose from pan-seared Patagonian lamb rack with chimichurri, fresh centolla (king crab) with garlic butter, or wild mushroom risotto. Paired with a premium Malbec.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic day of the trip. Weather in Torres del Paine is highly unpredictable – the guide will assess conditions at 03:00 before departure. Layers, waterproof jacket, and trekking poles are essential. Camera with extra batteries strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning. Optional yoga session on the resort's lakeside deck led by a private instructor, followed by a guided birdwatching walk around the resort's immediate shoreline – spot black-necked swans, upland geese, and steamer ducks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Valle del Francés (French Valley) Trek – Begin this spectacular half-day hike into the glacially carved French Valley amphitheater. Trek through ancient lenga beech forest with your private guide, ascending to viewpoints where hanging glaciers calve dramatically and condors circle overhead. The valley walls rise dramatically on all sides creating an awe-inspiring natural cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private hot tub soak under the Patagonian sky with a glass of champagne. The long December daylight (sunset near 22:00) provides spectacular evening light on the Paine Massif.

meals.breakfast: Healthy power breakfast at the resort – acai bowls, smoked salmon on sourdough, poached eggs, and green smoothies.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic in the French Valley – the resort prepares a premium hamper with aged cheeses, Patagonian lamb prosciutto, crusty bread, dried fruits, nuts, and a thermos of hot soup.
meals.dinner: Private chef's table dinner experience at the resort – a curated 6-course meal prepared tableside by the executive chef, featuring the best of Patagonian seasonal ingredients. Includes wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: The French Valley hike is moderately strenuous with significant elevation gain. Trekking poles highly recommended. Weather windows in December can shift quickly – waterproof layers are mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Multi-Day Hike – Day 1: Depart after an early breakfast with your private guide for the start of the iconic W Trek. Begin at the Laguna Amarga sector and trek toward Refugio Las Torres. The trail winds through open pampas with sweeping views of the Paine Massif, crossing rivers and spotting wildlife en route. Approximately 8 km today.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking toward the Las Torres base camp area, exploring the valley floor and glacier-fed rivers. Set up at a premium refugio or pre-arranged luxury camp with private tent accommodations, hot showers, and gourmet catering.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from the camp with the towers glowing in alpenglow. Stargazing session with the guide (December nights in Patagonia have very late, short darkness – expect light until ~22:30 and stars from ~23:00).

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the resort before departure – eggs, bacon, fresh bread, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch prepared by the private guide team – hot soup from a thermos, artisan sandwiches, energy snacks.
meals.dinner: Premium refugio dining or private camp dinner – hearty Patagonian stew, grilled lamb, fresh bread, and wine.

day_by_day.notes: This begins the 4-day W Trek segment. Luggage is kept at the resort; only a quality trekking daypack with essentials is carried. The resort arranges premium refugio or luxury camping accommodations along the route in advance. Confirm all bookings well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 2: Early rise for the Valle del Francés section from the western approach. Trek from Refugio Cuernos toward the French Valley lookout via the Mirador Británico trail. This is considered the most dramatic section of the W, with 360-degree views of hanging glaciers, the Cuernos del Paine, and deep valleys below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the French Valley and continue trekking toward Refugio Paine Grande. Approximately 12–14 km today with significant elevation change. Arrive at the refugio by late afternoon for rest and recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Communal refugio experience or private luxury tent with premium amenities. Enjoy the spectacular evening light on Lago Pehoé and the Paine Massif.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at the refugio – porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Trail lunch mid-hike – energy bars, sandwiches, fruit, and hot soup from thermos.
meals.dinner: Premium refugio dinner or private catered camp meal – pasta with Patagonian lamb ragù, fresh salad, and local wine.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the W Trek. An early start is essential. Weather conditions should be checked the night before with your guide. The Mirador Británico detour adds 3 hours but is absolutely worth it on a clear day.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 3: Depart Refugio Paine Grande toward Lago Grey. The trail follows the dramatic western arm of the W, with stunning views of turquoise Lago Pehoé giving way to the grey-blue expanse of Lago Grey. Trek approximately 11 km to the Grey Glacier viewpoint on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Grey with breathtaking views of the Grey Glacier face. Rest, take photos, and explore the shoreline where icebergs from the glacier drift into the lake. Optional short walk to the glacier viewpoint for close-up views of the ice face.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset over the Grey Glacier from the refugio terrace – one of the most dramatic sunset views in all of Patagonia. Celebrate the near-completion of the W Trek with a glass of Patagonian sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande – eggs, oats, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail near Lago Grey – gourmet sandwiches, cheese, dried fruit, and chocolate.
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Refugio Grey – grilled salmon, roasted vegetables, and a warm dessert with local calafate berry sauce.

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier views are extraordinary. Binoculars are recommended for glacier detail. Weather on this western section can be extremely windy – secure all loose items. This is the final overnight on the W Trek route.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek – Day 4 (Final): Early morning walk to the Grey Glacier viewpoint for sunrise colors on the ice. Begin the return trek back toward Refugio Paine Grande, completing the final leg of the W. Approximately 11 km return. Private vehicle transfer arranged by the resort meets the group at Paine Grande for a comfortable return journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by early afternoon. Indulge in a full luxury spa experience – deep tissue massage, hot stone therapy, and private sauna session to recover from four days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory W Trek completion dinner at the resort. Toast with Patagonian sparkling wine and enjoy a premium multi-course dinner in your honor.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Refugio Grey before departure – eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon return – fresh salads, soups, and sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Grand celebration dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – Patagonian king crab, aged lamb, and a premium dessert selection with a bottle of Gran Reserva Carménère.

day_by_day.notes: The W Trek is complete! This is a major achievement. Ensure spa treatments are pre-booked before the trek begins. Rest and recovery are the priority for the remainder of the day. Laundry service at the resort will handle all trekking gear.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast in bed, and take a leisurely stroll along the resort's private beachfront. Optional guided photography walk with the resort's in-house photographer to capture landscapes and wildlife in the soft morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition – Embark on this extraordinary private kayaking experience on Lago Grey. Paddle through iceberg-dotted turquoise waters toward the towering face of the Grey Glacier. Your expert guide provides full safety briefing and kayaking instruction. Get close to floating blue icebergs calved from the glacier – a truly once-in-a-lifetime Patagonian experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a hot shower and private jacuzzi session. Enjoy a curated cocktail hour featuring Patagonian gin infused with local botanicals.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed – full continental spread delivered to your suite with fresh-pressed juice, pastries, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the kayaking expedition – the resort prepares a waterproof-packed premium lunch with smoked fish, artisan bread, and hot soup in thermoses.
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner for two on the resort's private beachfront terrace – fresh centolla king crab, Patagonian lamb, and a decadent chocolate and calafate berry tart under the late evening Patagonian sky.

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking expedition requires moderate fitness but no prior kayaking experience. Waterproof dry suits are provided. December water temperatures are cold – all safety gear is supplied by the expedition team. Pre-book this experience well in advance as spots are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe near the park. Ride like a true gaucho across open pampas with views of the Paine Massif, spotting guanacos, condors, and native flora. A 2–3 hour premium experience arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the resort's private nature trail along the lakeshore. Visit the resort's wine cellar for a private sommelier-led tasting of premium Chilean and Argentine wines, perfectly timed for the festive evening ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at the resort – a lavish multi-course feast with live Andean folk music, premium wine and champagne, and traditional Patagonian holiday specialties. Dress code: smart casual elegance.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas Eve breakfast at the resort – smoked salmon blinis, fresh pastries, fruit platters, and sparkling wine mimosas.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's lakeside café – fresh salads, grilled fish, and homemade sourdough.
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner – six-course feast including Patagonian king crab cocktail, French onion soup, slow-roasted whole lamb asado, artisan cheeses, and a traditional Patagonian Christmas dessert with champagne toast at midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Patagonia is magical with extremely long daylight hours. The resort typically hosts a special gala event – confirm reservation and dress code with the concierge. This is a memorable cultural and culinary highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning sleep-in with a luxurious champagne breakfast delivered to your suite. Exchange gifts and enjoy the spectacular beachfront views from your private terrace. Optional gentle lakeside walk to appreciate the serene Patagonian Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat excursion on Lago Grey – cruise aboard the resort's private vessel through the iceberg-studded lake for close-up views of the Grey Glacier from the water. The guide shares insights on glaciology, climate change, and Patagonian natural history. Toast with champagne as you drift alongside ancient blue icebergs.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day sunset viewing from the resort's panoramic terrace with premium cocktails. Followed by a special Christmas Day dinner with festive decorations and a curated holiday menu.

meals.breakfast: Christmas champagne breakfast in suite – smoked salmon, caviar blinis, fresh croissants, tropical fruit, and a bottle of premium Moët & Chandon.
meals.lunch: Light festive lunch on the boat excursion – gourmet hamper with cold cuts, aged cheeses, artisan crackers, and sparkling wine.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Day dinner at the resort – traditional Patagonian asado (whole roasted lamb on the cross), accompanied by roasted vegetables, chimichurri, fresh salads, and a festive Patagonian berry pavlova for dessert, with premium wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Torres del Paine is one of the most spectacular days of the year – long light, peak summer conditions, and a magical atmosphere. The resort will have special holiday decorations and programming. This is a day to slow down and fully absorb the beauty of Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the resort's private beachfront – soak in the last views of the Paine Massif, the turquoise lake, and the Patagonian sky. Final gourmet breakfast at the resort's panoramic restaurant. Pack, settle any outstanding accounts with the concierge, and collect any purchased souvenirs or gifts from the resort boutique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs the resort for Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport. The resort concierge arranges a perfectly timed departure based on your outbound flight schedule. Enjoy a final look at the Patagonian landscape from the comfort of your private vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Patagonia with extraordinary memories of one of the world's last great wilderness destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final grand breakfast at the resort – full hot and cold buffet with every Patagonian specialty, freshly baked goods, and a farewell glass of calafate berry juice.
meals.lunch: Gourmet departure picnic box prepared by the resort chef – to enjoy at the airport or during transit, featuring local delicacies and Patagonian treats to take home.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight dining – the resort concierge can arrange VIP lounge access at Punta Arenas airport.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking gear is cleaned and packed the night before. The resort can arrange professional gear cleaning and packing service. Purchase calafate berry jams, Patagonian wine, and local artisan crafts as souvenirs from the resort boutique. Tip your private guide generously – 15–20% of guided experience costs is customary and greatly appreciated.
